title: HaramBlock DVR
description: Video session + DVR health, inference latency, anomaly dumps and umbrella traces for the HaramBlock extension (dev builds only).

panels.title: Health %
panels.description: Healthy windows / active windows. A 1 s window is healthy when playback is active, presented >= 0.9 x captured, no long task > 100 ms, no freeze and no audio underrun (probeCore.ts).

panels.title: Freeze seconds
panels.description: Active windows in which no new frame was presented (a paused video is not active, so never counts).

panels.title: Drops per minute
panels.description: captured - presented - repeated frames, per active playback minute. Catches sub-threshold skips the anomaly detector ignores.

panels.title: Audio fallback %
panels.description: Windows routed through relay or with audio unavailable, over all routed windows.

panels.title: Anomalies per 10 min
panels.description: video.dvr.anomaly dumps per 10 active playback minutes, comparable across sessions of any length.

panels.title: Warmup p90
panels.description: Time from DVR start to the first filtered frame (hb.dvr.warmup_ms, status ready).

panels.title: Captured vs presented fps
panels.description: Per 1 s window. Presented < 0.75 x captured for 2 s triggers a video.dvr.anomaly dump.

panels.title: Frame repeat ratio
panels.description: Share of presented ticks that re-served the previous frame.

panels.title: D (delay) over time
panels.description: DVR delay D. Steps up on video.dvr.delay_raised (cause verdict|store_stall).

panels.title: Capture time (ms)
panels.description: Per-tick frame capture cost (hb.dvr.capture_ms).

panels.title: Present time (ms)
panels.description: Per-tick present cost (hb.dvr.present_ms).

panels.title: Main-thread long tasks
panels.description: PerformanceObserver longtask entries while any DVR presents. > 100 ms during playback triggers an anomaly dump.

panels.title: DVR anomaly dumps
panels.description: video.dvr.anomaly headers plus their video.dvr.tick records (last 5 s per dump, one dump per 10 s per session). Expand a line for hb.dvr.tick.* (outcome new|repeat|miss, pinned, ring_span_sec, media_delta - negative is a source backstep) and the trace_id link.

panels.title: Playback active / verdict margin
panels.description: hb.dvr.playback_active is 1 while the presenter advances (0 = paused, ended or not yet warm). Verdict margin = D - observed round-trip p90: how far a presented frame's verdict lands ahead of its presentation; near 0 means unjudged frames are imminent.

panels.title: A/V drift (ms)
panels.description: hb.audio.drift_ms by route: relay = audio element vs currentTime - D (seeks past +-250 ms), delay line = DelayNode ramp vs wanted D.

panels.title: Frame drops / freezes per second (all sessions)
panels.description: Rollup counters by store/tap: dropped frames (captured - presented - repeated) and frozen windows.

panels.title: Healthy vs active windows per second (all sessions)
panels.description: Health % over time: healthy windows over active windows (hb.dvr.healthy_windows / hb.dvr.active_windows).

panels.title: Audio route windows / underruns (all sessions)
panels.description: Route distribution per period (hb.audio.route_windows by hb.audio.route) plus delay-line/relay underruns and unavailable windows.

panels.title: DVR runs started / stopped by reason, anomalies by cause (all sessions)
panels.description: Churn: hb.dvr.runs_started, hb.dvr.runs_stopped by hb.dvr.reason (seek, tap switch, source change...), hb.dvr.anomalies by hb.dvr.cause.

panels.title: Source vs captured fps
panels.description: Source fps = distinct mediaTime deliveries per 1 s window (rVFC callbacks or tap frames, duplicates excluded). Captured below source means the capture throttle or a skipped callback dropped frames before the ring.

panels.title: Capture vs native size (px)
panels.description: Width / height of the frame the DVR captures into the ring (hb.dvr.capture_width/height, the budget ladder tier actually applied) against the source geometry (hb.dvr.native_width/height). Capture above native is an upscale: wasted capture cost and ring bytes.

panels.title: Capture draw (ms)
panels.description: drawImage into the capture canvas, raw store only (hb.dvr.capture_draw_ms).

panels.title: Capture transfer (ms)
panels.description: transferToImageBitmap after the draw, raw store only (hb.dvr.capture_transfer_ms).

panels.title: Frame delivery gap (ms)
panels.description: Wall-clock gap between consecutive new-frame deliveries (hb.dvr.tick_gap_ms). Bands above the source frame interval mean the main thread delayed the callback; the Firefox substitute for the longtask observer.

panels.title: Deduped ticks (Firefox 60 Hz rVFC)
panels.description: Deliveries per 1 s window whose mediaTime equalled the previous one (hb.dvr.ticks_deduped). Firefox fires rVFC on every composited frame, so a 25 fps source shows ~35/s here; Chrome should be ~0.

panels.title: Source frames skipped / late ticks per second (all sessions)
panels.description: Skipped = mediaTime jumped more than 1.5 frame intervals between deliveries (the source advanced but no callback fired). Late = a delivery arrived more than 1.5 frame intervals after the previous one. By browser / store / tap.

panels.title: Sampler encode p50 / p90 and frames sent (content)
panels.description: Cost of bitmapToCompressedBlob (WebP) on the content main thread for the Firefox blob transport (hb.sampler.encode_ms), and inference frames sent per second by transfer kind (hb.sampler.frames_sent).

panels.title: Ring flushes / source backsteps per second (all sessions)
panels.description: hb.dvr.ring_flushes by cause (backstep: media time went backwards past the jitter tolerance; store: codec reconfiguration; swap: raw <-> encoded exchange) and hb.dvr.source_backsteps by size in frame intervals. A flush empties the ring: presentation pins until it spans D again (see pinned windows). Backsteps of 1-2 frames are the browser re-delivering an older frame, not a seek.

panels.title: Pinned vs frozen windows per second (all sessions)
panels.description: hb.dvr.pinned_windows: active windows in which the presenter held the earliest buffered frame because the ring did not yet span D (warm-up, re-warm, or a mid-run flush refilling). hb.dvr.freeze_windows for comparison: a freeze that is not pinned is a decode / present problem, a pinned freeze is a ring refill.

panels.title: DVR main-thread ms per second
panels.description: hb.dvr.main_thread_ms: capture + present time the DVR itself spent on the main thread per 1 s window (sum of the per-tick timings). 1000 is the whole budget; above ~400 the rVFC callbacks start arriving late and source frames are skipped. Sampler encode (Firefox WebP) is separate - see the sampler panel.

panels.title: Main-thread loop lag (ms)
panels.description: hb.main_thread.loop_lag_ms: drift of a 250 ms setTimeout while any DVR presents, sampled in the foreground tab only. Works on Firefox, which has no longtask observer; there a lag > 100 ms also trips the long_task anomaly and the health definition.

panels.title: Session + DVR events
panels.description: video.session.transition, video.dvr.start/stop/tap_changed/delay_raised/underrun/store_demoted/budget_*, video.audio.route, video.capture.failed.

panels.title: Inference round-trip (content) p50 / p90
panels.description: inference.roundtrip span duration as seen by the content script.

panels.title: Inference run (background) p50 / p90
panels.description: decode + preprocess + session.run per task.

panels.title: video.session umbrella traces
panels.description: One trace per VideoSession; video.dvr.warmup spans hang under it. Click a trace id to open it in Tempo; round-trips link to it via hb.session.trace_id.

panels.title: Slow inference round-trips (> 500 ms)
panels.description: inference.roundtrip traces whose root span exceeded 500 ms.
